a: Limit query depth to prevent deeply nested expensive queries.
Assign cost scores to fields and reject overly complex queries.
Disable or restrict introspection in production if not needed publicly.
Authorize at the field/resolver level, not only at the HTTP gateway.
Batched operations can amplify abuse; rate-limit and cap batch size.
Persisted/allowlisted queries reduce arbitrary query attack surface.
DataLoader batches and caches per-request DB lookups to fix N+1.
Do not leak stack traces or internal paths in GraphQL errors to clients.
Cap upload size and validate file types for GraphQL multipart uploads.
Treat public schemas as API surface: version carefully and monitor usage.
